clue.text: Not long ere a speaker's gift is turned to use at the bar

definitions.note: the definition names what the answer is for: a thing used by a barrister

indicators.note: ere is old poetic English for before, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: something not long is brief

indicators.note: is turned asks for the gift word to be read backwards in place

parts.note: the gift of the gab is a talker's fluency, so a speaker's gift is gab

explanation.surface: A short talk is a fine gift that a speaker can turn to good account in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is turned' sends GAB backwards to BAG. 'The bar' is the legal profession: a brief bag is the bag in which a barrister carries papers and robes.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief bag is the bag barristers carry their papers in, so it is something for use by the legal profession.

clue.text: Develop into suit

explanation.definitionFit: To become is to grow into something, and a garment that becomes you flatters or suits you.

clue.text: Heed not this wild region

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters of the region word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to this untamed territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges REGION.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no heed to something is to disregard it.

clue.text: Common Entrance — if not the commonest?

definitions.text: Common Entrance — if not the commonest?

parts.words: Common Entrance — if not the commonest?
parts.note: Common Entrance is the British exam for entry to public schools; read literally, it is the way into a house most people use

explanation.walkthrough: Common Entrance is the exam British children sit to enter private (public) secondary schools; here it is read as the usual way into a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The main entrance at the front of a house is the one most visitors use.

clue.text: They're a regular bind for the housewife

definitions.text: They're a regular bind for the housewife

parts.words: They're a regular bind for the housewife
parts.note: 'bind' is both a chore and a thing tied, and the ties of a kitchen pinafore are knotted on every day

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bind' is British slang for a tedious chore, but here it is literal: the ties of a pinafore bind it on. Being 'tied to' them also means being dominated by a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Apron strings are the ties that fasten a pinafore round the waist.

clue.text: Bob has to clear out plant

parts.note: bob is old slang for a shilling, abbreviated S in pre-decimal money
to purge is to clear out

explanation.surface: Bob is told he must dig out a plant from the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is the old slang word for a shilling, written S in British pre-decimal money (s for shillings).
explanation.definitionFit: Spurge is a genus of plants (euphorbia) with milky sap.

clue.text: City of cheese and violets

parts.note: an Italian city that gives its name to Parmesan cheese and to a sweet-scented violet

explanation.walkthrough: Parmesan cheese comes from the area of this Italian city, and Parma violets are a fragrant variety (and a British sweet).
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in Emilia-Romagna famed for Parmesan cheese, ham and violets.

clue.text: Always upset about damaged pier suspension

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the other piece
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for always is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: damaged suggests the letters of pier are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A damaged pier has been permanently closed off once again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EVER into REVE; 'damaged' scrambles PIER to PRIE; 'about' puts REVE round it, RE-PRIE-VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a suspension or postponement of a punishment.

clue.text: Facility of a chair

parts.note: facility means ease, and a comfortable armchair is an easy chair, so its quality is ease

explanation.walkthrough: 'Facility' means effortlessness, and the clue hints at the easy chair, whose defining quality is ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility means ease or lack of difficulty, the quality an easy chair is named for.

clue.text: Outlines a suggestion to students of travel brochures

parts.note: to con is to study, so 'con' is an instruction a student might be given
travel brochures advertise package tours

explanation.surface: Someone sketches out a tip for students reading holiday brochures.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart; addressed to students, 'con tours' tells them to study the tours.
explanation.definitionFit: Contours are the shapes or outlines of things, as of a coast or a figure.

clue.text: Disappointment may sour them

parts.note: Aesop's fox, failing to reach some fruit, declared it sour: disappointment makes the unreachable seem bitter

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'sour grapes' comes from Aesop's fable of the fox who, unable to reach the bunch, decided it was sour anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox's dismissal of fruit he could not reach gave English the idiom of sour grapes for a disappointed sneer.

clue.text: Too much of this from Hamlet's Player Queen, methinks

definitions.text: Too much of this from Hamlet's Player Queen, methinks

parts.words: Too much of this from Hamlet's Player Queen, methinks
parts.note: Gertrude watches the play-within-the-play and says 'The lady doth protest too much, methinks'

explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Queen Gertrude says of the Player Queen, 'The lady doth protest too much, methinks': her vows of loyalty are overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: A protestation is a solemn declaration or vow, like the Player Queen's over-insistent vows.

clue.text: Revolutionary start of a long race

indicators.note: start of means only the opening part of the race word is used, its ending dropped

parts.note: a marathon is a long-distance running race

explanation.surface: A rebel makes a fast start in a long-distance race.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution, stabbed in his bath in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: Marat was a radical journalist and politician of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Tusitala's job

parts.note: Tusitala, 'teller of tales', was the Samoan name for Robert Louis Stevenson, so his job is telling stories

explanation.walkthrough: The Samoans called Robert Louis Stevenson Tusitala, teller of tales; a teller of tales is engaged in storytelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Narration is the telling of a story, which is what a teller of tales does.

clue.text: Cavemen fatally jarred

parts.note: the robbers of Ali Baba's cave hid in oil jars and were killed there by Morgiana pouring boiling oil on them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavemen' are not prehistoric people but the robbers who used the cave in the Ali Baba tale; 'jarred' means put in jars, not jolted.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, Ali Baba's band of robbers hid in jars and were killed in them by the slave girl Morgiana.

clue.text: Strange origin can be revealed by this chemistry

indicators.note: strange means odd or altered, so the letters of origin can are rearranged

explanation.surface: Chemistry can reveal an odd source of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' scrambles ORIGIN CAN, and the result names the branch of chemistry the clue speaks of.
explanation.definitionFit: Inorganic chemistry is the branch studying substances other than carbon compounds.

clue.text: Sorted out by the fans

parts.note: fans are not supporters but blowers of air, which separate grain from chaff

explanation.walkthrough: The 'fans' are not enthusiasts but devices that blow air, which separates chaff from grain at threshing.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is winnowed when a current of air blows the chaff away from it.

clue.text: At the present time it's still a hanging matter

definitions.text: At the present time it's still a hanging matter

parts.words: At the present time it's still a hanging matter
parts.note: the present time is Christmas, gift time, when a child hangs up a sock to be filled with gifts

explanation.walkthrough: 'The present time' is gift-giving time, Christmas, when children hang up a long sock for presents; 'hanging matter' sounds like a capital crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas stocking is a long sock hung up on Christmas Eve to be filled with presents.

clue.text: No minister is worried by a break

indicators.note: worried means harassed or shaken about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A government minister is never troubled by a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is worried' shakes up the letters of NO MINISTER IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermission is an interval or pause in a performance.

clue.text: In transport lies the rub, coming up to Town from here

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer as the place a commuter travels up to Town from

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from the bottom, so the whole assembly is reversed
in places the rub inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a bus is a means of transport
taken as written, the word rub

explanation.surface: Hamlet's 'there's the rub' finds a home on a bus to London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts RUB inside BUS, making BRUBUS; 'coming up' turns it, as the down entry is read upwards. 'Town' is London, which one goes 'up' to.
explanation.definitionFit: A suburb is an outlying residential district from which commuters travel into the city.

clue.text: The screen mysteriously diffuses the odour of sanctity

definitions.note: the definition describes what the answer does, a verb phrase standing for the object that spreads holy fragrance

indicators.note: mysteriously suggests the letters of screen are rearranged in an unexplained way

explanation.surface: Incense drifts through a church screen with a holy scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysteriously' scrambles SCREEN. The 'odour of sanctity' is the smell of incense, which a swinging censer spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: A censer is a vessel swung in church services to spread the smoke of burning incense.

clue.text: Return in a vehicle to Spanish Water in Central America

definitions.note: the definition names the region the answer lies in, a country of that isthmus

indicators.note: return asks for the short word beside it to be read backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
agua is the Spanish word for water

explanation.surface: A traveller drives back to a place called Spanish Water in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns IN round to NI; 'Water' is capitalised to look like a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicaragua is a Spanish-speaking republic on the isthmus between Mexico and Colombia.

clue.text: Panic splashing here by the river

definitions.text: Panic splashing here by the river

parts.words: Panic splashing here by the river
parts.note: Panic means of the god Pan, who in Browning's poem splashed among riverside plants and made pipes from them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Panic' means belonging to Pan: E. B. Browning's 'A Musical Instrument' has the great god Pan 'down in the reeds by the river', splashing and cutting a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are tall water grasses growing by rivers, from which Pan cut his pipes.

clue.text: Measure the vocal challenge

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the word for challenge is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: a gage is a pledge or glove thrown down as a challenge

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a singing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: A gage is a glove thrown down as a challenge to fight; it is pronounced like the measuring word.
explanation.definitionFit: To gauge is to measure or estimate an amount.

clue.text: He also serves

parts.note: Milton wrote 'They also serve who only stand and wait': a restaurant server both serves and waits

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on Milton's line 'They also serve who only stand and wait': the person who waits at table literally serves.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant waiter serves food and drink to diners.

clue.text: The freeborn grow in pride

parts.note: Born Free told of the lioness Elsa; young lions grow up within a pride, the word for a group of lions

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' is the group noun for lions, not self-esteem, and 'freeborn' nods to Born Free, the book and film about the lioness Elsa.
explanation.definitionFit: Young lions are raised within a pride, the family group of lions.

clue.text: Assimilate into a body of laws?

explanation.surface: Lawmakers absorb something into a legal code.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest is to absorb or take in, and a digest is a compendium of laws, like Justinian's Digest of Roman law.

clue.text: It might drop a point, to serve wine instead of sandwiches

definitions.text: It might drop a point, to serve wine instead of sandwiches

parts.words: It might drop a point, to serve wine instead of sandwiches
parts.note: dropping the compass point N from a place selling quick food leaves a bar serving sack, an old sherry-like wine

explanation.walkthrough: Remove the N (north, a point of the compass) and the place becomes a 'sack bar', where sack is the old fortified wine Falstaff drank.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack bar is a counter or small café selling sandwiches and light meals.
